subject: physical-education

location.unitTitle: Lifetime Activity Audit and Adult Transition Planning
location.courseTitle: Lifelong Wellness and Independent Training Capstone

standardsMappingAuthority.note: Standards remain governed by the bound production package.

instructions: Complete the safe activity or accessible equivalent and document the requested performance evidence.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing trouble, unsafe conditions, or missing adult supervision.

learnerTasks.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of auditing current activities against post-graduation reality in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe time, money, transport, facility, and social access after high school using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply what disappears when school activity structures end in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving activities that require nothing but space and time; correct it and explain why.
Connect building a minimum viable activity week with setting a realistic first-year activity commitment and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Audit every activity the learner currently does against post-graduation constraints, then design a minimum viable activity week that would survive the worst plausible version of next year.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

learnerSuccessCriteria: Provide evidence that meets the stated safe participation and self-management criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated skill cues or movement quality criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated tactical or training reasoning criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated self-assessment and revision criterion.
accommodations: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.

provenance.unitObjective: How can the learner demonstrate the goals of Lifetime Activity Audit and Adult Transition Planning?
